text.en:
A rational number can be written as p by q where p and q are integers and q is not zero. An irrational number cannot be written like this.
The textbook first proves a helping result: if a prime p divides a squared, then p divides a.
To prove that root 2 is irrational we use contradiction. Suppose root 2 = a by b, where a and b have no common factor other than 1.
Squaring gives 2 b squared = a squared, so 2 divides a squared and therefore 2 divides a. Write a = 2c.
Then 2 b squared = 4 c squared, so b squared = 2 c squared and 2 divides b as well. Now 2 divides both a and b, which contradicts our assumption that they have no common factor.
So our assumption was wrong, and root 2 is irrational. The same method proves that root 3 and root 5 are irrational.
The sum or difference of a rational and an irrational number is irrational. The product or quotient of a non-zero rational and an irrational number is irrational.
Be careful: the sum of two irrationals can be rational. For example root 2 and minus root 2 add up to 0.

Suppose 3 + 2 root 5 is rational, equal to a by b with b not zero.
Then root 5 = (a - 3b) / 2b, and the right side is rational.
But root 5 is irrational, a contradiction. So 3 + 2 root 5 is irrational.
